questions.stem: Which of the following is an operating system?
questions.explanation: Windows is an operating system — system software that manages hardware and provides a platform for applications. MS Word (word processor), Google Chrome (browser), and Photoshop (image editor) are all application software that run ON an operating system. Other OS examples: Linux, macOS, Android, iOS.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Software that is designed to harm or disrupt a computer is generally called:
questions.explanation: Malware (malicious software) is any software designed to harm, disrupt, or gain unauthorised access to a computer. Types include viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware, and spyware. Freeware is free software; shareware is trial software; firmware is software embedded in hardware.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: The two broad categories of software are application software and:
questions.explanation: Software is broadly divided into two categories: (1) System software (operating systems, device drivers, utilities) that manages the computer itself, and (2) Application software (Word, browsers, games) that performs specific tasks for users. The OS is the most important piece of system software.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following is an open-source operating system?
questions.explanation: Linux is an open-source operating system — its source code is freely available for anyone to view, modify, and distribute. It powers most servers, Android phones, and supercomputers. Windows and macOS are proprietary (closed-source). Distributions (distros) include Ubuntu, Fedora, and Debian.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which operating system is most widely used on smartphones globally?
questions.explanation: Android, developed by Google and based on the Linux kernel, is the most widely used smartphone operating system globally. Apple's iOS is the second most popular. Windows Phone, BlackBerry OS, and Symbian are largely discontinued mobile operating systems.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: A program that translates high-level programming language code into machine code all at once is called a:
questions.explanation: A compiler translates the entire high-level source code into machine code in one go, producing an executable file. An interpreter translates and runs code line by line. An editor is for writing code, a debugger finds errors, and a linker combines object files into a single executable.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which type of malware disguises itself as legitimate software to trick users into installing it?
questions.explanation: A Trojan horse (or Trojan) disguises itself as legitimate or useful software to trick the user into installing it, then performs malicious actions. Unlike a virus or worm, it does not self-replicate. A worm spreads automatically across networks; adware shows unwanted ads; a rootkit hides deep in the system to evade detection.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What is the primary function of an operating system?

options.text: To manage hardware resources and provide a platform for application software

questions.explanation: The primary function of an operating system is to manage the computer's hardware resources (CPU, memory, storage, I/O devices) and provide a platform/interface on which application software runs. Key OS functions include process management, memory management, file management, and device management.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Ransomware is a type of malware that:

options.text: Encrypts the victim's files and demands payment for the decryption key

questions.explanation: Ransomware encrypts a victim's files (or locks the system) and demands a ransom payment, usually in cryptocurrency, in exchange for the decryption key. Notable examples include WannaCry and Petya. Defences include regular backups, software updates, and not opening suspicious attachments.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following is system software, NOT application software?
questions.explanation: A device driver is system software that allows the operating system to communicate with hardware devices (printer, graphics card, etc.). VLC Media Player, WhatsApp, and MS Excel are all application software that perform specific user tasks. Drivers, utilities, and the OS itself are system software.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What does 'booting' a computer mean?

options.text: The process of starting up the computer and loading the operating system into memory

questions.explanation: Booting is the process of starting up a computer, during which the BIOS/UEFI runs a power-on self-test (POST) and loads the operating system into RAM. A 'cold boot' starts from power-off; a 'warm boot' (restart) reboots without fully powering down. The term comes from 'pulling oneself up by the bootstraps'.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Software available free of cost but with the source code kept proprietary (not modifiable) is called:
questions.explanation: Freeware is software available free of charge, but its source code is NOT open for modification (it remains proprietary), e.g., many free utilities and readers. Open-source software (like Linux) provides free access to the source code. Shareware is free for a trial period before requiring payment.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which utility program reduces the size of files to save storage space?
questions.explanation: A file compression tool (like WinZip, 7-Zip, or WinRAR) reduces file size to save storage and ease transfer, creating archives such as .zip or .rar. An antivirus detects malware; a disk defragmenter reorganises fragmented data on a hard disk; a firewall controls network traffic.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of application software?
questions.explanation: VLC Media Player is application software — it performs a specific task for the user (playing media). The Linux kernel, device drivers, and BIOS are all system software that manage or interface with the hardware. Application software runs on top of system software.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: A 'firewall' in computer security is used to:

options.text: Monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules

questions.explanation: A firewall is a network security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules, acting as a barrier between a trusted internal network and untrusted external networks (like the internet). Firewalls can be hardware-based, software-based, or both.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which key combination is commonly used to force-open the Task Manager in Windows to close unresponsive programs?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Alt + Delete brings up a security screen in Windows from which the Task Manager can be opened to close unresponsive programs (Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager directly). Alt + F4 closes the active window; Windows + L locks the screen.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which company developed the Windows operating system?
questions.explanation: Microsoft, founded by Bill Gates and Paul Allen, developed the Windows operating system (first released 1985). Apple develops macOS and iOS; Google develops Android and Chrome OS; IBM developed OS/2 and early PC-DOS. Windows is the most widely used desktop OS.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What is a 'patch' in software terms?

options.text: A piece of hardware added to a computer
A software update that fixes bugs or security vulnerabilities

questions.explanation: A patch is a piece of software designed to update, fix bugs in, or address security vulnerabilities of an existing program or its supporting data. Regular patching is a key cybersecurity practice. A collection of patches is sometimes bundled as a 'service pack' or 'update'.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In an operating system, 'multitasking' refers to:

options.text: The ability to run multiple programs/processes seemingly at the same time
Connecting multiple computers in a network

questions.explanation: Multitasking is an operating system's ability to run multiple programs/processes seemingly simultaneously by rapidly switching the CPU between them (time-sharing). On multi-core processors, true parallel execution also occurs. Running multiple OSes is 'dual-booting' or virtualisation; networking computers is a separate concept.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes 'antivirus' software?

options.text: Software that detects, prevents, and removes malicious software
Software that speeds up internet browsing

questions.explanation: Antivirus software detects, prevents, and removes malware (viruses, worms, trojans, etc.) from a computer. It uses signature-based detection, heuristic analysis, and real-time scanning. Examples include Norton, McAfee, Kaspersky, and Windows Defender. Keeping antivirus definitions updated is essential.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes a virus from a worm?

options.text: A virus needs a host file/program and user action to spread; a worm self-replicates and spreads across networks independently
A worm needs a host file; a virus spreads on its own
Both are identical and the terms are interchangeable
A virus only affects hardware; a worm only affects software

questions.explanation: A virus attaches itself to a host file or program and typically requires user action (running the infected file) to activate and spread. A worm is standalone malware that self-replicates and spreads automatically across networks without needing a host or user action. This independence makes worms spread far faster (e.g., the ILOVEYOU and WannaCry incidents).
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What is 'virtual memory' in an operating system?

options.text: Extra RAM physically installed in the computer
A technique where part of the hard disk/SSD is used as an extension of RAM when physical memory is full
Memory used only by virtual reality applications

questions.explanation: Virtual memory is a memory-management technique where the OS uses a portion of secondary storage (hard disk/SSD), called the page file or swap space, as an extension of RAM when physical memory is full. This lets the system run larger programs than physical RAM alone would allow, though disk access is much slower than RAM (causing 'thrashing' if overused).
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What is the role of a 'device driver' in an operating system?

options.text: It physically drives the cooling fans
It is software that enables the OS to communicate with and control a specific hardware device
It connects the computer to the internet

questions.explanation: A device driver is specialised system software that acts as a translator between the operating system and a specific hardware device (printer, graphics card, network adapter), enabling the OS to send commands to and receive data from that device. Without the correct driver, the hardware may not function or function poorly.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: In OS process management, what is a 'deadlock'?

options.text: When the computer is switched off abruptly
A situation where two or more processes are each waiting indefinitely for resources held by the others, so none can proceed
When a file is permanently deleted
When the antivirus quarantines a file

questions.explanation: A deadlock occurs when two or more processes are each holding a resource and waiting for a resource held by another, creating a circular wait so that none can ever proceed. The four necessary conditions (Coffman conditions) are mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and circular wait. Operating systems use prevention, avoidance (e.g., Banker's algorithm), or detection to handle deadlocks.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which statement about open-source versus proprietary software is correct?

options.text: Open-source software always costs more than proprietary software
Open-source software makes its source code freely available for anyone to view, modify, and distribute, whereas proprietary software keeps its source code closed and restricts modification
Proprietary software is always free of cost
Open-source software cannot be used commercially

questions.explanation: Open-source software (e.g., Linux, Firefox, LibreOffice) makes its source code freely available to view, modify, and redistribute, often under licences like GPL or MIT. Proprietary software (e.g., Windows, Adobe Photoshop) keeps its source code closed and legally restricts modification/redistribution. Open-source is frequently free but CAN be used commercially; cost and openness are separate dimensions.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
